To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the wood-decaying fungal community composition determines the efficiency of wood decomposition and the pattern of volatile organic compound release.
fungal decay type and fungal interactions determine decomposition of spruce and release of volatile compounds from the wood.

(1) the decay type of wood-decaying fungus, either white or the brown rot, determines the efficiency of wood decomposition and the pattern of volatile organic compounds released upon fungal growth; (2) the decay type is reflected by enzyme activities and accumulation of oxalate; and (3) the decay type can be predicted by a combination of enzyme activities and volatile organic compounds released.

the effect of fungal decay type on wood decomposition and VOC release in solid state cultivation.

fungal interactions and enzyme activities are the main drivers of wood decomposition.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
wood decomposition is a highly regulated process, and it is controlled by the fungal species combination and the enzyme activities produced.
wood decomposition is a complex process involving multiple interactions between wood components and fungal metabolites.
wood decomposition and release of VOCs depend on fungal decay type, fungal interaction and enzyme production patterns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
wood decomposition patterns, as determined by mass losses, enzyme production patterns and release of volatile organics, depend on both decay type of fungi and fungal interactions.
the combination of fungal decay type, growth conditions and fungal interactions can be used as a tool for biotechnological applications, for instance in bioremediation of wood-based materials.
